topic.readerProblem: Someone searching 'AI SEO' or 'AI for SEO' does not know whether it means using AI tools in SEO work or optimizing to be named by AI engines, and needs to know how to do both well without publishing scaled thin content.
topic.connection: AEOeye audits whether ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity recommend a brand; this page defines both meanings of AI SEO, points the optimization half to AEOeye's AEO guide, and uses AEOeye's crawler access study and its own 2026 content clean-up as first-hand evidence.

assessment: The page defines AI SEO as two jobs (AI as a tool, AI as the audience) in a table, then shows where AI genuinely helps SEO work (clustering, gap briefs, merge candidates, schema drafts, crawl QA), where it hurts (scaled content abuse per Google's spam policy, hallucinated facts, unreviewed decisions), how to optimize for AI answers (index and snippet eligibility, retrieval-bot access, answer-first passages, off-site mentions, click reality), a weekly workflow and a category-level tools table. It rests on Google Search Central documentation, Pew browsing data, the GEO paper, OpenAI crawler documentation and AEOeye's crawler study (n and sample caveat stated) and clean-up history. It deliberately does not claim any engine rewards AI-written content or specific schema, quotes no vendor prices, and does not say the retired posts were AI-generated.

sources.supports: Last updated 2026-10-01: generative AI can be useful when researching a topic and to add structure to original content; using it to generate many pages without adding value may violate the scaled content abuse policy; generative models predict likely word sequences rather than retrieve facts and can hallucinate; fact-check content including title elements, meta descriptions, structured data and alt text.

Last updated 2026-08-28: scaled content abuse is many pages generated for the primary purpose of manipulating rankings and not helping users, no matter how created; examples include using generative AI tools to generate many pages without adding value.

No additional requirements to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode; a page must be indexed and snippet-eligible; no new machine-readable files, AI text files, markup or special schema.org data needed; AI-feature traffic is reported in Search Console's Performance report within the Web search type.
Last updated 2026-10-01: in the attributes quality raters evaluate, using generative AI to produce large amounts of text without manual oversight represents little to no effort.
Structured data policy: do not mark up content that is not visible to readers of the page; the markup must describe the same content the HTML body shows.
Google Search Console is described as a free service that helps monitor, maintain and troubleshoot a site's presence in Google Search.

Browsing data from 900 US adults, March 2025: a traditional result was clicked in 8% of visits with an AI summary versus 15% without; a link inside the summary in 1% of visits; Wikipedia, YouTube and Reddit made up 15% of sources listed in AI summaries.
GEO paper abstract: GEO methods can boost visibility by up to 40% in generative engine responses on the authors' GEO-bench, and efficacy varies across domains.

OAI-SearchBot surfaces sites in ChatGPT search; opted-out sites will not be shown in ChatGPT search answers though they can still appear as navigational links; OAI-SearchBot and GPTBot settings are independent.
Lists AEO, LLMO, AIO and AI SEO as other terms for the same concept as generative engine optimization.
Defines AI hallucination as plausible-sounding falsehoods generated by a model, including fabricated citations; used to define the term on first use.

Microsoft's February 2026 announcement of the AI Performance report in public preview, showing how publisher content is cited across Microsoft Copilot, AI-generated summaries in Bing and select partner integrations.
